hero.tagline: An impressionist journey through light, philosophy & the cosmos

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: In many cultures, the new moon is considered a time for planting seeds — both literal and metaphorical. Darkness is not emptiness; it is the womb from which light is born.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: Arrogance is the ego's armor. But armor is heavy — it slows the warrior. The Gita teaches that true strength comes not from the assertion of self but from the surrender to dharma.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: The Gita was spoken on a battlefield, not in a temple. Wisdom does not require perfect conditions. The most profound truths are often revealed in the midst of chaos, not in the silence of retreat.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: Shiva is called Tryambaka — the three-eyed one. The third eye represents the eye of wisdom that sees beyond the duality of good and evil, self and other, creation and destruction. When it opens, the universe is consumed in flame — not as punishment, but as liberation.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: Waves are the ocean's way of communicating with the shore. Each one is unique, yet all are the same water. Identity is like a wave — real in its moment, eternal in its substance.
